subtitle: When Cannons Met the Emperor’s Seal

panels.shot: split-composition wide, half a smoky battlefield at Buxar, half a dim hall with a Mughal emperor sealing a document
panels.action: On one side, Hector Munro stands amid cannon-smoke over a field of scattered guns; on the other, Shah Alam II, weary yet regal, presses his seal to a Persian farman under the arches of Allahabad.

dialogue.text: In 1764, at Buxar, muskets spoke; in 1765, at Allahabad, ink flowed. Between Hector Munro’s guns and Shah Alam II’s seal, a trading company quietly became a tax‑collecting power over millions.

i18n.hi: १७६४ में बक्सर पर बंदूकें गरजीं, १७६५ में इलाहाबाद पर कलम चली। हेक्टर मुनरो की तोपों और शाह आलम द्वितीय की मुहर के बीच, एक व्यापारी कम्पनी चुपचाप लाखों की महसूलदार बन गई।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a large wall map of eastern India lit by flickering lamplight
panels.action: Hector Munro studies a map showing the Ganga, Patna and Buxar, while in another corner of the frame a faint, translucent image of Shah Alam II sits in a makeshift camp near Allahabad, his tent lit by a small lamp.

dialogue.text: After Plassey, Bengal did not fall in a single stroke. It tottered for years, between nawabs, bankers and a Company that still pretended to be only a trader.

i18n.hi: प्लासी के बाद बंगाल एक वार में नहीं गिरा। सालों तक नवाबों, साहूकारों और खुद को सिर्फ व्यापारी कहने वाली कम्पनी के बीच डगमगाता रहा।

panels.shot: medium wide inside a nawab’s durbar, slightly low angle to show hierarchy
panels.action: In a crowded court, Mir Qasim argues fiercely with English factors over account scrolls, while Shuja-ud-Daula stands thoughtfully to one side and a dignified but travel-worn Shah Alam II listens from a modest seat, the imperial parasol absent.

dialogue.text: Mir Qasim, the new nawab of Bengal, quarrelled with the Company over duties and trade privileges. In Awadh, Shuja-ud-Daula watched uneasily. Shah Alam II, emperor without a capital, sought a path back to power.

i18n.hi: नए बंगाल नवाब मीर क़ासिम की कम्पनी से लगान और सुभीदा पर ठन गई। अवध में शुजा-उद-दौला चिंतित नज़र रखे थे। राजधानी से बेदखल बादशाह शाह आलम द्वितीय फिर ताक़त की राह खोज रहे थे।

panels.shot: dynamic oblique overhead of marching columns converging along the Ganga
panels.action: Long lines of Mir Qasim’s troops, Shuja-ud-Daula’s contingents and the emperor’s modest imperial force march along dusty roads towards the Ganga, banners of Bengal, Awadh and the Mughal crescent fluttering together in the heat.

dialogue.text: In 1764, their interests met in one decision: to challenge the Company in open field. The nawab of Bengal, the nawab of Awadh and the Mughal emperor formed a fragile coalition, marching towards Buxar on the Ganga.

i18n.hi: १७६४ में सबकी दिलचस्पी एक फैसले पर मिली—मैदान में कम्पनी को सीधी चुनौती। बंगाल का नवाब, अवध का नवाब और बादशाह ने नाज़ुक गुट बनाया और गंगा किनारे बक्सर की ओर कूच किया।

panels.shot: low-angle medium on Munro on horseback against a hazy dawn
panels.action: Hector Munro sits calm on horseback near the British lines at Buxar, his European officers around him, sepoy battalions in ordered ranks behind, the early light catching neat rows of artillery.

dialogue.text: Facing them stood Hector Munro with a much smaller force, but drilled battalions and well‑served guns. His dispatches speak of discipline, steady volleys and the quiet confidence of men used to line and file.

i18n.hi: उनके सामने था हेक्टर मुनरो, फौज कम, पर कड़ी तरबीयत और चुस्त तोपख़ाना। उसकी रिपोर्टों में अनुशासन, थमी हुई गोलियां और कतारों के आदी सिपाहियों का बेफिक्र भरोसा झलकता है।

panels.shot: wide panoramic battlefield shot, slightly elevated, capturing both armies at the moment before engagement
panels.action: Across flat fields near Buxar, the allied army stretches in a long, uneven arc, cavalry restless at the wings, while the Company line stands compact and rectangular, cannons forward, both sides facing across a smoky no-man’s-land.

dialogue.text: On 22 October 1764, near Buxar, the armies drew up. Ghulam Hussain Khan later wrote of a coalition strong in numbers but loose in command, confronting Company troops whose strength lay in cohesion more than in size.

i18n.hi: २२ अक्तूबर १७६४ को बक्सर के पास दोनों फौजें आमने-सामने खड़ी हुईं। ग़ुलाम हुसैन ख़ान ने बाद में लिखा—जोड़ में मजबूत, पर कमान में ढीला गुट, ऐसे सिपाहियों से भिड़ा जिनकी ताक़त संख्या से ज्यादा एकजुटता थी।

panels.shot: tight, dramatic three-quarter view of allied guns firing, smoke rolling across
panels.action: The allied coalition’s cannons roar, crews straining at the wheels, thick smoke drifting toward the Company line, while distant silhouettes of Mughal and Awadhi infantry advance hesitantly behind the gun line.

dialogue.text: Guns opened first. The coalition fielded many pieces, yet coordination faltered. Munro’s own records recount how his artillery answered methodically, each shot part of a measured pattern rather than a scattered roar.

i18n.hi: पहली दहाड़ तोपों की थी। गुट के पास तोपें तो बहुत थीं, तालमेल कमज़ोर। मुनरो के कागज़ बताते हैं कि उसका तोपख़ाना नाप-तौल कर जवाब देता रहा—हर गोला एक पैटर्न में, बिखरी दहाड़ नहीं।

panels.shot: medium wide on Munro and sepoys firing volleys, slight low angle to emphasize discipline
panels.action: Hector Munro raises his sword in a crisp signal as sepoy ranks fire controlled volleys, muskets levelled in unison, while officers pace behind them, keeping the line straight amid drifting powder smoke.

dialogue.speaker: hector_munro_and_shah_alam_ii
dialogue.text: Steady, men. Fire by platoons—hold the line.

i18n.hi: हौंसला रखो, सिपाहियो। पलटन-पलटन फायर करो—कतार मत तोड़ो।

panels.shot: wide shot of allied line beginning to waver, seen from behind their ranks
panels.action: From behind the coalition front, allied infantry are shown wavering and drifting back, some officers gesturing urgently, while in the distance Company bayonet lines advance, their formation still tight through the haze.

dialogue.text: As the day wore on, cohesion broke on the allied side. The Siyar ul-Mutakhkhirin remembers confusion and sudden retreats. Munro reported the opposing line giving way, their guns and camp left exposed.

i18n.hi: दिन बढ़ते-बढ़ते जोड़ की तरफ़ से डोर टूट गई। सियार-उल-मुतअख्खिरिन में अफ़रा-तफ़री और अचानक भागते दस्ता दर्ज है। मुनरो ने सामने की कतार टूटने, उनकी तोपें और डेरा खुला छूटने की खबर की।

panels.shot: dramatic ground-level shot of abandoned artillery and a disordered camp, with the Company in the background
panels.action: The image shows rows of heavy cannons abandoned near a sprawling camp of struck tents and scattered equipment, as Company soldiers move in orderly fashion among them, the Ganga glinting beyond.

dialogue.text: By evening, the coalition was routed. British records claim 133 guns taken and rich cash stores seized. However we weigh their figures, the result is clear: the nawab of Awadh and the emperor could no longer dictate terms by force.

i18n.hi: शाम तक गुट पूरी तरह बिखर गया। अंग्रेज़ी रेकॉर्ड १३३ तोपें और भारी नक़दी हाथ लगने का दावा करते हैं। गिनती जैसी भी हो, नतीजा साफ़ था—अवध का नवाब और बादशाह अब ज़बरदस्ती शर्तें मनवा नहीं सकते थे।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Shah Alam II in a quiet tent after defeat, lantern light casting long shadows
panels.action: Shah Alam II sits on a simple carpet in a modest tent, his face thoughtful and lined, a scribe kneeling nearby with papers, while outside, a few remaining attendants stand guard in a subdued camp.

dialogue.text: For Shah Alam II, Buxar was another bitter turn. Once emperor in name, now defeated ally, he had seen Delhi lost and now watched another hope fall at the Ganga’s edge. His path would turn from sword to seal.

i18n.hi: शाह आलम द्वितीय के लिए बक्सर एक और कड़वा मोड़ था। कभी नाम के बादशाह, अब हारे हुए हमसफर; दिल्ली हाथ से जा चुकी, अब गंगा किनारे एक और आस ढहती दिखी। उनका रास्ता तलवार से मुहर की ओर मुड़ गया।

panels.shot: wide view of Allahabad fort and confluence, majestic, from a distance at sunset
panels.action: The massive walls of Allahabad fort rise at the meeting of the Ganga and Yamuna under a glowing sky, small boats clustered below, while tiny figures move along the ramparts hinting at the preparations within.

dialogue.text: In 1765, the road led to Allahabad, where the Yamuna meets the Ganga. There, under Company protection, the emperor set up his camp, and negotiations began that would bind Bengal’s revenue to a foreign corporation.

i18n.hi: १७६५ में राह उन्हें इलाहाबाद लाई, जहाँ यमुना गंगा से मिलती है। वहीं कम्पनी की हिफ़ाज़त में बादशाह ने डेरा डाला, और बात-चीत शुरू हुई जिसने बंगाल की आमदनी एक विदेशी कम्पनी से बाँध दी।

panels.shot: medium interior of a formal meeting hall within Allahabad fort, balanced two-shot of Munro and Shah Alam II
panels.action: Inside a vaulted hall, Shah Alam II sits on an elevated but modest seat, attendants behind him, while Hector Munro stands respectfully before him, hat under his arm, a folded document held by a Company official nearby.

dialogue.speaker: hector_munro_and_shah_alam_ii
dialogue.text: Between us, Majesty, the pen must now finish what the sword began.

i18n.hi: हम दोनों के बीच, हुज़ूर, अब तलवार नहीं, कलम काम पूरा करेगी।

panels.shot: close-up on a scribe’s hands writing Persian script on thick paper, with seals and ink nearby
panels.action: A Mughal scribe carefully inscribes elegant Persian lines on a large sheet, next to a tray of red wax and imperial seals, while the faint figures of Company representatives and imperial officers blur in the background.

dialogue.text: The Treaty of Allahabad took shape in careful script. One key clause granted the English Company the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa—the right to collect revenue in the emperor’s name, for an annual payment to his court.

i18n.hi: इलाहाबाद की सन्धि सधे हुए लफ़्ज़ों में ढली। एक अहम धारा में अंग्रेज़ कम्पनी को बंगाल, बिहार और उड़ीसा की दीवानी मिली—बादशाह के नाम पर वसूली का हक, बदले में दरबार को सालाना अदायगी।

panels.shot: tight, reverent close-up of Shah Alam II’s hand pressing his seal on the document
panels.action: Shah Alam II’s ringed hand presses the imperial seal onto the treaty, the wax gleaming soft red, as Hector Munro watches from the side, his face composed but intent.

dialogue.text: On 16 August 1765, the emperor affixed his seal. In form, he remained sovereign. In practice, he granted a private company the fiscal lifeblood of three rich provinces, in exchange for tribute and protection.

i18n.hi: १६ अगस्त १७६५ को बादशाह ने अपनी मुहर लगा दी। काग़ज़ पर वो मालिक रहे, पर अमल में उन्होंने तीन सूबों की खून-सी आमदनी एक निजी कम्पनी को दे दी—नज़र और हिफ़ाज़त के बदले।

panels.shot: medium shot of Munro and Company officials examining revenue ledgers and maps, slight overhead
panels.action: Hector Munro stands with Company officials over a table strewn with maps of Bengal and bound revenue ledgers, their fingers tracing rivers and district names, as a window behind them shows the Ganga far below.

dialogue.text: From Fort William’s records we see what followed: surveys, new collectors, streams of coin redirected to Company treasuries. Buxar’s battlefield victory became, through Allahabad’s treaty, a steady claim upon land and labour.

i18n.hi: फ़ोर्ट विलियम के रेकॉर्ड दिखाते हैं आगे क्या हुआ—नक़्शे, नए कलेक्टर, सिक्कों की धाराएँ कम्पनी के ख़ज़ानों की ओर मुड़ती हुई। बक्सर की फतह इलाहाबाद की सन्धि से ज़मीन और मेहनत पर टिकाऊ दावा बन गई।

panels.shot: somber medium on Shah Alam II in his Allahabad camp, gazing toward the river, profile view
panels.action: Shah Alam II stands at the edge of his camp, looking out thoughtfully over the river, the faint glow of Allahabad fort behind him, his posture dignified yet heavy with reflection.

dialogue.text: Ghulam Hussain Khan saw in these years an emperor forced to trade authority for survival. For Shah Alam II, the diwani grant was both necessity and loss: a way to draw revenue, but also an admission of altered power.

i18n.hi: ग़ुलाम हुसैन ख़ान ने इन सालों में एक ऐसा बादशाह देखा जो ज़िंदा रहने को इख़्तियार बेचने पर मजबूर था। शाह आलम द्वितीय के लिए दीवानी देना ज़रूरत भी थी, नुक़सान भी—आमदनी का ज़रिया, मगर घटती ताक़त का इक़रार।

panels.shot: broad, time-lapse style bird’s-eye composite over Bengal’s countryside, hinting at future changes
panels.action: A sweeping view over Bengal’s green fields, rivers and bustling towns gradually fades into overlayed silhouettes of Company buildings and flags, while small figures of peasants and zamindars stand below, dwarfed by the new structures.

dialogue.text: Plassey had placed a nawab under Company influence, but Buxar and Allahabad gave formal, imperial sanction to Company revenue rights. A battlefield decision rippled into the daily lives of cultivators, traders and zamindars across the delta.

i18n.hi: प्लासी ने एक नवाब को कम्पनी के ताबे कर दिया, पर बक्सर और इलाहाबाद ने कम्पनी के महसूल हक़ को बाकायदा बादशाही मंज़ूरी दी। मैदान का फ़ैसला डेल्टा भर के किसानों, सौदागरों और ज़मींदारों की रोज़मर्रा ज़िंदगी तक लहर बन कर पहुँचा।

panels.shot: split close-up of Munro’s weathered face fading into Shah Alam II’s lined visage, both looking in opposite directions
panels.action: Hector Munro’s face, stern and worn by campaign, overlaps with Shah Alam II’s thoughtful profile, the background dissolving into a faint outline of the Treaty of Allahabad and the word ‘diwani’ in stylised Persian script.

dialogue.text: Buxar did not end in a single victory cry; it ended in a signature that turned battle into bookkeeping. In Munro’s volleys and Shah Alam’s seal, we see how, in 1765, a ledger quietly took the place of a throne.

i18n.hi: बक्सर का अंत एक जंगी नारे पर नहीं, एक दस्तख़त पर हुआ—जिसने जंग को हिसाब-किताब में बदल दिया। मुनरो की गोलियों और शाह आलम की मुहर में दिखता है कैसे १७६५ में ख़ज़ाने की किताब ने चुपचाप तख़्त की जगह ले ली।
